atoms.a: Why do we use quotation marks?
b: ++to write something that someone else said

hint.text:
1. If you introduce a quote, place a comma at the end of the introduction. The first word inside the quote is capitalised.
2. If you open with a quote, place a comma at the end of it before explaining who was quoted.
3. If your quote is an exclamation or question, use an exclamation mark or question mark instead of a comma.
4. If the introduction to your quote is a full sentence, you can use a colon instead of a comma.

b: “Do you like to paint”? he asked me.
++“Do you like to paint?” he asked me.
++The lawyer did not want to give any details on the case: “No comment!”
The lawyer did not want to give any details on the case “No comment”.
++“Oh man,” he sighed. “Why won’t it turn on?”
“Oh man”, he sighed. Why won’t it turn on?
++Val giggled at the cartoon in the magazine: “Darren, come look at this!” she exclaimed.
“Val giggled at the cartoon in the magazine Darren, come look at this!” she exclaimed.
